claims.text: The feedstock is pre-alloyed AlCrFeNiSi powder with a particle-size distribution suitable for powder-bed fusion.
Maintaining the build substrate at approximately 500°C during laser powder-bed fusion will reduce residual thermal stresses.
Substrate preheating will produce a more homogeneous microstructure than conventional processing without preheating.
Substrate preheating will improve the mechanical properties of miniature AlCrFeNiSi components relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
The proposed substrate-temperature processing window is 450–550°C, with approximately 500°C as the target.
The proposed intervention applies to miniature components with characteristic dimensions below 10 mm processed in an inert atmosphere.
Laser power and scan speed must be adjusted under preheated conditions to stabilize the melt pool.
Substrate preheating reduces the thermal gradient between the melt pool and the build platform.
Reduced thermal gradients mitigate rapid cooling.
Mitigating rapid cooling decreases dislocation density.
Mitigating rapid cooling decreases phase heterogeneity.
The reduced thermal differential causes more gradual solidification.
More gradual solidification produces more uniform phase transformation.
The controlled thermal environment reduces sharp internal stress gradients.
Reduced internal stress gradients and more uniform phase transformation minimize defects that degrade mechanical properties.
Preheated components will have higher tensile strength than non-preheated controls.
Preheated components will have greater tensile ductility than non-preheated controls.
Preheating will reduce processing complexity by producing fewer defects and a more uniform phase distribution.
The intervention's effectiveness may vary with feedstock thermal properties, build system, and feedstock batch.
A failure to achieve at least a 20% residual-stress reduction together with improved tensile properties and microstructural uniformity would falsify the hypothesis.
